questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: Culturally, Paris interested me as a city with its rich history, numerous cultural offers and shere size. Academically, the exchange - as part of the electives - gave me the possibility to explore a new subject/area of research.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I expected much worse given the complaints of previous exchange students. I think especially in the beginning it is important to let go of your need for control at least a little bit and trust that everything is going to work out - in the end, the partner university, too, is interested in making a good impression on their exchange students.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a one-week language course as well as a formal introductory meeting and a more informal welcoming cocktail event.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Luckily, I was offered an apartment in one of the Crous residences. French students are queuing up for these so if you are given the option of one of the apartments I would advise to take it - especially for the low rent.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: Paris is a well-connected city, so I do not consider this a problem.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: The course registration was honestly chaotic. Of course, the initial learning agreement did not work out due to overlaps and limited admission. Students are responsible themselves for checking the compatibility of courses. The course registration took place online and was based on "first-come, first-serve".

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Panthéon-Sorbonne has a dedicated coordinator who serves as guidance to the exchange students. He is generally happy to help but possibly had to many issues to resolve and was thus not always quick to reply.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: In the end, I am happy with the course selection but it definitely warrants a certain flexibility from the students' side.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: To stay relaxed. In case you do not get admitted to a course, you can possibly ask personally whether they can make for an additional spot.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: 3rd year Bachelor courses, Master 1 courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The teaching quality was, in my opinion, inferior to the academic standard I am used to from Denmark and Germany. I found it irritating sometimes that the professors insisted on their authority and treated some students badly and not as equal discussion partners (if ever they let a discussion happen to begin with).

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
International Monetary Economics 
Urban Economics 
Economics of Education 
France and the EU
Resources and Climate Change

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Urban Economics

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: If you know the right places, the cost of living is considerably cheaper than in Copenhagen especially in terms of going out.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Various sport courses and a French language course.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I will always recommend sport courses - also as a way to actually speak applied French with other students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Lots of museums, parks, concerts, restaurants and bars leave, in my opinion, no time for boredom.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: I think you need to develop a bit of a "hard shell" and let not everything reach you personally. Otherwise, I greatly enjoyed the French attitude.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Sport courses, coffee breaks during the lectures.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Generally, people - in power positions - insist on their authority. However, I noticed that the administration always sounds much harsher than the actual practice is.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Affordable restaurants, buzzing streets and very clean parks.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: First, to not choose the university for academic ambitions (only) but for the greater environment you find in Paris. Second, to bring some flexibility and trust that the administration will help you eventually. Third, to prepare for the exam period in early January in good time - otherwise it gets very stressful during and after the Christmas holidays.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: nA

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting other (exchange) students and finding your way in a new city.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: I personally struggled with my courses quite a bit. This was partly due to the fact that I have never studied Economics before but also due to very long (3 hours usually) and ill-structured lectures.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
